BUCK.bench

a talking white-tail trophy you print, wire and hang on pegboard. an SG90 servo swings the jaw; an ESP32-S3 or RP2040-Zero and the NULLLAB NS4168 kit (amp and its 3W speaker) do the talking from inside the neck; one USB-C cable runs out the back. everything else is printed: eyes, nose, ears, antlers, pivot pin and pegboard hooks. every part is one material, so print each in its own filament or print it all in one and paint it.
1 head

sculpt, eyes, nose, ears, antlers

2 guts

servo jaw, boards, speaker, wiring

3 mount

plaque, edge, pegboard hooks, head screws

4 print

fit audit, filaments, plates, 3MF

pick a starting point; every change rebuilds the parts and reruns the fit audit.

EYES + NOSE

x

separate eyes are almond domes that press into sockets inside the lids; print them in black for a real shine. sculpted puts them in the head for painting. fit is the designed clearance per side; holes print about 0.15 small, so 0.10 gives a light press.

ANTLERS

x
x
round on top and 45 degrees underneath, so they print flat with no supports and still look round. keyed tenons press into the pedicles.

EARS

x
ears print lying on their flat backs, cup up: the back is a flat plane with a steep bevel to the rim, and the tenon runs down to the bed, so nothing hangs in the air.

JAW

deg
mm
mm
channel: the lower jaw is an even skin opened through the mouth like a real one, a U trough with a thicker lip rim and the tongue groove down the middle (about 47 percent less plastic). sealed keeps a solid mouth face over a closed void. both print mouth face down with no support: the trough floor is tented at 45 degrees to an 8 mm bridge. the hinge, arms, horn groove and pin bore stay solid.
the jaw rides the servo horn on the right and a printed pivot pin on the left, both on one axis. it slides up through the mouth onto the horn, then the pin pushes in through the left cheek and clicks. no screws: the arm's groove keeps the horn on the spline.

BOARDS

the controller sticks onto a plinth on the left face of the fin with foam tape or hot glue. the plinth is 9 mm wide, narrower than the pin rows, so every pin and edge pad stays free to solder. its USB-C faces the plaque and lines up with the cable slot.
i2s amp: NULLLAB NS4168, 38.4 x 22.4 from the vendor drawing. it lies flat on a shelf above the speaker on two posts whose spigots fill its 4.7 mm holes, held by two M3 x 6 screws. it slides in from the servo horn side, input connector first, so the fin over it is cut back only where that end passes.

SPEAKER

mm
mm
mm
mm
mm
mm
the kit speaker lies face down on a seat ring in the bottom of the neck and fires down through a grille in the throat. its ears screw to two bosses with M2 pilots. these sizes come off the listing photo, not calipers: measure yours and set frame, ear span and depth, and the seat, bosses and shelf follow.

WIRING

pins are a suggestion; any free GPIO works. on an S3 keep off strapping pins 0, 3, 45 and 46. the amp's input is the 5 pin PH2.0 lead from the kit: G, V, BCLK, LRCLK, DIN.

PLAQUE

mm
of width
mm
the plaque is sized off the neck: neck fill is how much of the plaque width the neck takes. the edge profile is cut in whole layers so it prints exactly.
3 screws: the head slides over the locating lip and three M3 x 16 flat head screws go in from the back of the plaque, countersunk flush, into bosses inside the neck rim (one top, two low). to take the head off, slide the plaque off its hooks and undo three screws. snap: the old two bead snap, no hardware, less secure.

PEGBOARD

in
mm
printed hooks are curved prongs: hold one tilted up, put the tip in a hole and roll it down, and it locks behind the board. do two, a whole number of inches apart, then slide the plaque's back channel onto both from the side. the head's weight winds them tighter.

FIT AUDIT

FILAMENTS

per filament: one 3MF per spool, each a plate you print on its own. one colour: everything packed onto as few plates as possible, then paint; the paint view is your guide.

slicer profile
names only, never settings. blank leaves the slicer's selection alone.
no supports anywhere: head rim down, jaw on its mouth, plaque on its back, nose on its cut face, eyes on their backs, ears lying cup up, antlers, pin and hooks flat. parts are nested on their real footprints, so in one colour mode everything goes on a single 256 bed. exports always use the fine mesh.
